mcq_fix.s: Consider the following statements about early railways in South India: 1. The first railway in South India was run by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway. 2. The first railway in South India ran from Royapuram (Madras) to Wallajah Road (Arcot) on 1 July 1856. 3. The first railway line in Andhra was Puttur-Renigunta, in 1862. Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcq_fix.why: statement 1 'That line' had no referent; answer unchanged (Madras Railway ran it)

mcq_drop.why: odd assertion-reason with no causal link either way; ambiguous
dubious: Atmiya Sabha date disputed (1814/1815) and Hindu College credit contested

pyq_bad.why: garbled: stem is a pasted explanation block

patterns: APPSC asks this area mainly via education policy one-liners: Macaulay's 'single shelf' remark (APPSC G2 2025), Downward Filtration = education (APPSC G2 2024), year pairs Wood 1854 / VPA 1878 / Factory Act 1881 / Famine Code 1883.

Other PSCs repeat first-railway facts (1853, Bombay-Thane, GIP Railway, Dalhousie) and newspaper-founder pairs (Mirat-ul-Akhbar, Al-Hilal, Qaumi Awaz, Hindoo Patriot/Harish Chandra Mukherjee, Amrita Bazar Patrika turning English).
Chronology items mixing press laws with other Acts are a recurring shape.
App MCQs add strong AP angle (Telugu journals, Puttur-Renigunta) which is appropriate, but some Telugu-press items are obscure versus PYQ depth.
